FAQs
EARLY CHECK-IN / LATE CHECK-OUT
Our standard check-in time is from 3:00pm, with check-out at 11:00am. Each room is carefully prepared following departure to ensure it is presented at its very best for your arrival.
For guests wishing to arrive earlier, we are pleased to offer early check-in, subject to availability:
From 11:30am: Half-day room rate
From 1:00pm: £50 early check-in fee
We also offer a late check-out until 12:00pm for £25, subject to availability.
As early check-ins and late check-outs require us to adjust our housekeeping schedule, availability cannot be guaranteed. We recommend arranging either in advance with our team, who will be happy to assist in making your arrival and departure as relaxed and seamless as possible.
Can the venue accommodate the ceremony
Yes, our venue can certainly accommodate your ceremony needs. We are pleased to inform you that our space can accommodate up to 250 people, ensuring ample room for your guests.
Is the venue licensed?
Yes, our wedding venue is fully licensed. We take pride in offering a comprehensive service that includes all necessary licenses and permits to host your wedding ceremony and reception.
What is your alcohol policy?
Our venue is fully licensed for alcohol and entertainment. As per our policy, all alcohol must be sourced from the venue only.
Is there parking available?
Yes, parking is available at our venue with EV charging available.
Can we schedule a tour of the venue before booking?
We would be delighted to show you around the castle to ensure all of your questions are complete. Please reach out to weddings@otterburn.uk
Do you provide assistance with wedding planning and coordination?
Our wedding team provides on-site coordination of our in-house services for food, beverage, and furniture. For additional services, our team will happily provide recommendations for suppliers including wedding planning and wedding co-ordination.
Are there any restrictions on decorations or entertainment?
Absolutely not! This is your fairy tale, and we want to ensure it's everything you've ever dreamed of. Whether you envision an extravagant display of florals, twinkling fairy lights, or lively entertainment to enchant your guests, we're here to bring your vision to life without limitations. Your imagination sets the stage; we're here to make it a reality.
Important notes to read
Our outside sound curfew is set at midnight to ensure a serene and respectful atmosphere for all.
The Elopement Disclaimer
Our elopements offer a full experience reminiscent of a Las Vegas elopement—fun, exclusive, impulsive, and thrill-seeking.
**Please note that these experiences are not official weddings.
We can recommend Celebrants for your elopement or alternatively, you are welcome to invite your own preferred.

Otterburn Castle
0
HISTORY
A Thousand Years of Legend and Legacy
Founded in 1086 by a cousin of William the Conqueror, Otterburn Castle began its life as a Norman stronghold guarding England’s volatile northern frontier. For centuries, it served as both a defensive bastion and a symbol of power along the Anglo-Scottish border. In 1388, the surrounding lands bore witness to the legendary Battle of Otterburn, a pivotal clash during ongoing border conflicts. Scottish forces, led by James Douglas, known as the “Good Sir James,” engaged an English army under Henry “Hotspur” Percy. Though both commanders were captured, the Scots emerged victorious in what became one of the most iconic battles of medieval chivalry—later immortalized in ballads and chronicles across Europe. Ownership of the estate later passed to Clan Hall, before the current castle structure was built in 1830 by Thomas James, a magistrate who used stones from the original medieval fortress to reconstruct the estate in its current Gothic Revival form. Officially recognized for its architectural and historical significance, Otterburn Castle became a Grade II listed building on 7 January 1988. Today, Otterburn Castle is a private estate open to the public as a boutique hotel, event venue, and culinary destination. While its walls whisper the stories of centuries past, its future is being reimagined—where history meets modern hospitality, and every guest is invited to write their own chapter in its enduring legacy.

wikipedia.title: Otterburn Tower
wikipedia.extract: Otterburn Tower is a Grade II listed castellated, three star country house hotel in Otterburn, Northumberland. It is set in 32 acres (13 ha) of deer park and woodland in the Northumberland National Park in northeastern England. Founded by a cousin of William the Conqueror in 1086, it was later owned by the Clan Hall, before being rebuilt in 1830 by Thomas James, a magistrate, on the site and using some of the stones from Otterburn Castle. Nearby Otterburn Hall was built in 1870 on land given to a Lord Douglas as recompense for the death of his ancestor James Douglas, 2nd Earl of Douglas in the Battle of Otterburn.
